newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf producers brace for Tropical Storm Danny.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf producers brace for Tropical Storm Danny.

text.p: Oil and natural gas producers braced for heavy rains and high winds as Tropical Storm Danny formed in the Gulf of Mexico, officials said.
Texaco Inc moved about 100 workers back to shore and prepared for more extensive evacuations if the storm intensified and moved deeper into oil and gas fields in the central Gulf, a spokesman said.
"We're pulling about 100 non-operating personnel off various rigs and platforms," spokesman Pierre DeGruy said. "We're on standby alert status on other platforms, but no production is shut in.
Shell Oil Co said no production had been shut in from its offshore platforms, and the company had no plans early Thursday to evacuate offshore crews.

Crews on offshore rigs and production platforms were battening down ahead of the system, which buffeted some elevated platforms in the northern Gulf with tropical storm level winds of more than 39 miles an hour overnight.
The storm at 1000 CDT was located near latitude 28.3 north, longitude 91.9 west and drifting northeast at about 5 miles an hour with maximum sustained winds of 50 miles an hour.

Danny was on track to make landfall Friday morning along the Mississippi Delta in Louisiana, and a tropical storm warning and hurricane watch were raised from Cameron, La., to Orange Beach in east Alabama.

"By this time tomorrow we're expecting Danny to have strengthened to at least a strong tropical storm, possibly a minimal hurricane before it has a chance to move onshore," said Wilkens Weather Technologies meteorologist Marshall Wickman.
The Houston-based weather service was predicting landfall south of Port Fourchon, La., on the east side of Timbalier Bay, about 25 miles southwest of Houma.
The storm flared up from a lazy tropical depression this morning as it moved into warmer, shallower water and found lighter winds aloft near the coast.
Winds also were rotating clockwise at the top of the weather system, improving outflows at the top and aiding circulation on the surface, he said.
